startup.name: Normal
startup.one_liner: Applied research lab for hardware design
startup.description: Normal is described only as an applied research lab for hardware design, tagged Hardware, Manufacturing, AI and Industrial, with a team of 4 in San Francisco in the Summer 2025 batch. No description was given, so I assume it builds AI tools or models that help engineers design and manufacture physical parts, sold to hardware and manufacturing companies.

yc_acceptance.basis: Already in the Summer 2025 batch, so reported for completeness. Start at the roughly 1 percent prior, lift for a four person team and the AI for hardware engineering theme that fits YC interest, and take nothing for traction because none is stated and the description is empty.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: YC would most plausibly say no because AI for CAD and hardware design already had YC companies (Adam W25, camfer S24, Hestus S24, Draftaid W24), and a research lab framing with no stated customers or product gives no evidence that the team has a wedge that pays.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --years 2022-2024 --industry Industrials: seed 51% / 55% / 59%, cond 55% (n=85). Timing: time_to_milestones.csv industry:Industrials months_to_seed p25 3, p50 6, p75 22.1.
anchors.adjustment_reason: The anchor of 0.55 is the ever reached figure. The window is 16 months from 2025-07-07 to 2026-11-17; Industrials seed timing has a median of 6 months and p75 of 22, so roughly 65 to 70 percent of eventual raisers are inside it, about 0.37. I make no lift for the AI hardware theme, because the winners test showed such lifts did not separate winners from the rest. The odds do not rank this company against others.

bands.rationale: Small post YC round of $1M to $3M, typical when a two to four person team raises from angels and micro funds soon after demo day. Hardware design tools such as Hestus raised a small first seed of $1.5M in early 2025 and Adam raised $4.1M later, so the low and middle bands are most likely.

Institutional seed of $3M to $6M, near the 2022 and later median of $3.5M in round_benchmarks.csv, which includes the YC deal so it reads low. Hardware design tools such as Hestus raised a small first seed of $1.5M in early 2025 and Adam raised $4.1M later, so the low and middle bands are most likely.
Larger institutional seed of $6M to $12M, where press covered 2026 raises had their median of $6.0M; needs live revenue or a standout founder story.
Upside seed above $12M, seen in 2025 voice, document and agent categories when a lab style team is bid up by several funds.

ladder.why_it_fails: Investors want an AI hardware design product with design customers, and a research lab framing with no stated product leaves them nothing to price. Companies in the same wedge raised small first rounds (Hestus $1.5M) or ended inactive (camfer, Hestus peers) before bigger seeds, so the most likely failure is that the team stays at the YC deal or a sub $1M check.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --years 2022-2024 --industry Industrials: series_a cond 30% (n=47), ever 16% known-only, range 15% to 23%.
anchors.adjustment_reason: The anchor is the ever reached figure. The forecast window is 16 months from the as of date, and months_to_series_a in time_to_milestones.csv has a median near 28 to 35 months, so only a small share of eventual Series A raisers get there inside the window. Hence the probability is well below the anchor.

bands.rationale: Thin or small Series A, common for vertical software with early but modest revenue.
Central band around the 2022 and later Series A median of $15M with p25 $11M.
Strong growth round led by a top tier fund.
Upside where the category is hot and revenue compounds fast.

ladder.why_it_fails: A Series A needs repeat paying engineering customers and a product that survives CAD vendors' own AI features. In the months after a seed the team would need to turn a research lab into a revenue business, which few hardware tool startups did. Adam raised a seed more than half a year after batch and has not shown an A, so the A inside the window is unlikely.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --years 2022-2024 --industry Industrials: series_b cond 7% (n=14), ever 1% known-only.
anchors.adjustment_reason: Series B inside a window of 16 months is rare: months_to_series_b has a median of 36 to 47 months from the batch start in time_to_milestones.csv, so almost no company reaches it this fast. Only a breakout would.

bands.rationale: Thin Series B or extension round, used when growth slowed after the Series A and investors price the company on revenue multiples alone.
Central band; 2022 and later Series B median is $40M.
Hot company band; 2022 and later post money median is $600M.
Breakout upside where one lead investor competes hard for a category leader with fast revenue growth and strong net retention.

ladder.why_it_fails: A Series B inside the 16 month window would need breakout revenue in a market where AI CAD tools are still early. No hardware design AI company in the records has done it, so this is a tail case where several funds back a category winner.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --years 2022-2024 --industry Industrials: series_c cond 0% (n=1), ever 0% known-only.
anchors.adjustment_reason: The anchor is conditional on Series B, ever reached. Inside the window almost nobody gets to Series C, and I keep the figure low and nonzero for a breakout path with several quick rounds.

bands.rationale: Thin extension or flat round, used when growth slowed after the Series B and investors price the company on revenue multiples alone.
Central band; 2022 and later Series C median is $74M.
Strong growth round led by a large crossover or growth fund after the company shows durable revenue and net retention above 110 percent.
Category leader upside where the company is among the top two in its market and raises at a premium multiple to scale internationally.

ladder.why_it_fails: Series C inside the window is almost out of reach. The Industrials cohort has essentially no company reaching it in this time, and the category is early, so only an extraordinary customer and revenue ramp with multiple large rounds back to back would produce it.

outcomes.why_it_fails: The likely outcome is a stall or small acquisition because AI for hardware design is a feature that Autodesk, Dassault and Siemens can absorb. Camfer (S24) is flagged inactive, Draftaid took only a small round, and Symplex (S19), a research lab, was acquired by Scale AI, which shows research teams often end as acquihires.

analogs.outcome_summary: Went viral at launch, raised a $4.1M seed in October 2025, about eight months after batch.
Raised $1.5M in January 2025 and a $7.4M seed in 2026, showing a small first round then a larger one.
Flagged inactive by YC though the site was live, with only YC money found.

analogs.relevance: Winter 2024 3D model to CAD drawings with AI
analogs.outcome_summary: Paid pilots but only a small YC level round found.
Listed as acquired by Scale AI with no public details.

killers.evidence: Autodesk, Dassault and Siemens own the CAD workflow and announced AI assistants, so a standalone design tool is easy to absorb.
killers.mitigation: Build models trained on proprietary manufacturing data that incumbents lack.

killers.risk: Research lab with no revenue product
killers.evidence: The input describes a research lab and gives no product, customers or pricing, so investors have no revenue to underwrite.
killers.mitigation: Ship a narrow paid tool for one part type within the batch.

killers.evidence: Manufacturers have long design and qualification cycles and low software spend, which slows pilots to contracts.
killers.mitigation: Sell to fast moving hardware startups first.

technical_complexity.rationale: Generating valid parametric geometry and manufacturing aware designs needs models that understand geometry, constraints and process rules, which is research grade. A four person research team can reach a demo, but integration with CAD tools and trust from engineers take longer.

takeover_risk.rationale: Incumbent CAD vendors have the user base and already ship AI assistants, so a standalone design model can be copied or bundled within a year unless Normal owns data or a niche that incumbents do not serve.

evidence.claim: Several AI mechanical engineering startups raised seed rounds in 2025, showing investor demand
Hestus raised a seed to cut repetitive CAD tasks, showing engineers will use plugins

brand.name: Normal
strengths: Short, real word and easy to say
weaknesses: Impossible to search and says nothing about hardware design
brand.rationale: A short real word like Normal is easy to remember and has an understated tone, but it is generic to search for and does not signal hardware; past YC real word names such as Vapi style brands show distinctiveness helps, though outcome depends more on the product.

narrative.headline: A thinly described AI hardware design lab in a funded but incumbent-exposed category; a priced seed inside 16 months is somewhat above one in three.
narrative.general_summary: Normal is an applied research lab for hardware design with a team of four. The input has no description, so the forecast rests on the tags and one line. AI for CAD and manufacturing drew many YC companies and several seed rounds in 2024 and 2025, but also inactive ones, and incumbents such as Autodesk and Dassault own the workflow. For the 16 month window I use the Industrials cohort timing for seed with no lift for the AI theme, per the winners test. A Series A inside the window is unlikely. The odds do not rank Normal against other companies, and a small first round of $1M to $3M is the most likely size if it raises.

assumptions: Only the input file was used about the company; the description was empty so the product is assumed from the one liner and tags.
Seed means a round above about $1M from outside investors, not the standard YC deal.
Search results dated after 2025-07-07 were treated as market context for other companies only.
